body.p: The Office Action issued on August 29, 2024, has been received and its contents carefully considered. Claim 1 is the independent claim, and claims 1-4 and 6-12 remain pending in the application. For at least the following reasons, it is submitted that this application is in condition for allowance.
Claims 1-4 and 6-12 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Geiger (WO 2020123833).
The Applicant respectfully traverse the rejection of claim 1. Claim 1 recites:
a plurality of modules that are coupled together, wherein each of the plurality
of modules includes:
a first link;
a second link movably linked to the first link; and
a liquid pressure cylinder configured to move the first link and the second link
relative to each other by a working fluid that is supplied to a cylinder chamber from a
liquid pressure source located outside the plurality of modules and is discharged
from the cylinder chamber to a tank located outside the plurality of modules, wherein
the first link includes a cylinder block in which the cylinder chamber of the
liquid pressure cylinder is formed, the cylinder block having a plurality of outer
surfaces, and at least two of the plurality of outer surfaces of the cylinder block each
have both a pump port connectable to the liquid pressure source and a tank port
connectable to the tank.
(emphasis added)
The Examiner considers that Geiger discloses every elements recited in claim 1.
Applicant respectfully disagrees since there are at least seven reasons (#1)-(#7) why Geiger does not disclose the claimed invention, as explained hereinafter.
[E} The Examiner has equated actuator units 30A, 30B of Geiger to the plurality of modules of claim 1. FIGs. 1, 3 and 9 of Geiger are duplicated below.
In Geiger,
[0025] Ankle actuator system 17 actuates foot 19 relative to lower leg 18 at joint 20.
Ankle actuator system 17 includes two side-by-side electro hydrostatic actuators
30A and 30B. Referring now to FIG. 9, in a first embodiment actuator 30A of actuator
system 17 is schematically indicated as including variable speed bidirectional electric
servomotor 31A, bidirectional or reversible pump 32A driven by motor 31 A, and
double-acting hydraulic piston assembly 33A. Actuator 30B of actuator system 17 is
schematically indicated as including variable speed bidirectional electric servomotor 3
IB, bidirectional or reversible pump 32B driven by motor 31B, and double-acting
hydraulic piston assembly 33B. (emphasis added)
FIG. 9
As shown above, however, the actuators 30A, 30B are "two side-by-side electro hydrostatic actuators 30A and 30B" and are thus not configured to be coupled together.

(5). Moreover, the Examiner has equated pumps 32A, 32B to the claimed liquid pressure source. As shown in FIG. 9 of Geiger, the actuator 30A includes pump 32A therein. Thus, since the pumps 32A, 32B of Geiger are included inside the actuators 30A, 30B, Geiger does not teach or suggest "a liquid pressure cylinder configured to move the first link and the second link relative to each other by a working fluid that is supplied to a cylinder chamber from a liquid pressure source located outside the plurality of modules," as recited in claim 1.

6) Further, the Examiner has referred to para 0028 of Geiger and states that the features recited in a wherein clause are disclosed in Geiger. However, Geiger merely states "one side or port 42 of each pump 32A, 32B communicates with left chamber 35A, 35B via fluid line 44, respectively, and the opposite side or port 43 of each pump 32A, 32B communicates with right chamber 36A, 36B via fluid line 45, respectively," and thus ports 42 and 43 are ports of pumps 32A, 32B, and thus formed inside the actuators 30A, 30B. Therefore, Geiger does not teach or suggest "at least two of the plurality of outer surfaces of the cylinder block each have both a pump port connectable to the liquid pressure source and a tank port connectable to the tank," as recited in claim 1.
27). Geiger also discloses connections ports 48A, 48B, and states as follows:
[0029] In this embodiment, oil reservoir 41 compensates for thermal oil expansion and
contraction within the systems and is controlled by check valves 46A and 46B.

Connection ports 48A and 48B are used to fill the system with oil. Line 49 provides a pump casing leakage relief conduit to reservoir 41. The electrohydraulic actuator is a closed hydraulic system in that fluid is not supplied to the system from an external
source in operation. Nor is fluid permitted to drain to an external sump in
operation. Rather, reservoir 41 is either discharged or recharged, as appropriate, to
accommodate differential fluid volumes. Motors 31 A and 3 IB are required to provide
torque and consume power when motions work against gravity. (emphasis added)
As is clear from the above, since Geiger is a closed hydraulic system, "fluid is not

supplied to the system from an external source in operation Nor is fluid permitted to drain to an external sump in operation." That is, Geiger clearly does not disclose or teach "a liquid pressure source located outside the plurality of modules," "a tank located outside the plurality of modules," and "at least two of the plurality of outer surfaces of the cylinder block
each have both a pump port connectable to the liquid pressure source and a tank port connectable to the tank," as recited in claim 1.

Accordingly, Geiger does not teach or suggest all of the features recited in claim 1 and thus does not render claim 1 obvious. Claims 2-4 and 6-10 depend from claim 1 and are thus patentable over the cited references for at least the reasons advanced above as to the patentability of claim 1. Therefore, the rejection of claims 1-4 and 6-10 should be reconsidered and withdrawn.
Based on the above, it therefore is submitted that this application is in condition for

allowance and a notice to that effect is requested. Should the Examiner feel that a conference would help to expedite the prosecution of this application, the Examiner is hereby invited to contact the undersigned counsel to arrange for such an interview.
No fee is believed due. Should any fee be required, the Commissioner is hereby
authorized to charge the fee to our Deposit Account No. 18-0002, and is respectfully requested to advise us accordingly.
Respectfully submitted,
